descriptionChirho: Hifil causative: to actively destroy, annihilate, or exterminate a people, nation, or entity -- the agent deliberately causes total destruction. Cross-linguistic evidence uniformly supports a single causative sense: Arabic uses active forms of IV-stem roots abad (أَبَادَ) and ahlaka (أَهْلَكَ) interchangeably; Korean consistently uses 멸하다 (to destroy/exterminate); Swahili uses kuangamiza (active destruction); Hindi uses nash karna (destroy) and nasht karna. The Arabic variation between abad/ahlaka/dammara reflects translator choice, not polysemy. Includes all Hifil inflections: perfect, imperfect, imperative, infinitive construct, infinitive absolute, consecutive imperfect, and forms with pronominal suffixes and prepositional prefixes.

Nifal passive: to be destroyed, perish, or be exterminated -- the entity undergoes annihilation rather than causing it. Cross-linguistic evidence clearly distinguishes this from the Hifil: Arabic uses passive forms ubida (أُبِيدَ), yubadu (يُبَادُ), yuhlaku (يُهْلَكُ); Korean uses 멸망당하다/멸망하다 (suffer destruction, perish) vs. the active 멸하다; Swahili consistently uses the passive kuangamizwa vs. the active kuangamiza; Hindi uses nash hona (be destroyed) vs. nash karna (destroy). Includes all Nifal inflections: perfect, imperfect, infinitive construct, infinitive absolute, and waw-consecutive forms.
